text: [W9 item 1 - READING] The cluster is NOT gear down and NOT thermal: it is the Cummins TORQUE MANAGEMENT fuel limiter (e2m Torque_Mgmt_*), the transmission-protection fuel limit keyed on the drivetrain gear ratio. CODE: cm848_runTorqueManagement (called from cm848_periodicTaskSet_protection, cpp 6873) builds a fuel quantity limit from a requirement flag (cm848_evaluateTorqueManagementRequired: transmission_type_cal, vehicle_speed, drivetrain_ratio, transmission_current_gear), a table limit (rpm table, stage 0-2 = the 4-D fuelling tables at a throttle breakpoint), an entry ramp down (limit = previous fuel demand or limit minus a step until it reaches the table limit), an exit hold timer and an exit ramp up (limit + step until above fuel_demand_computed + offset); the limit goes into the running fuel limit protection_fuel_limit_active with source code 45 (0x2d) and straight into the min() of cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit. e2m (corroboration, nine consecutive words, same roles and the same scale in each): Torque_Mgmt_Delay_Time / Manual_GR / Neg_Slew_Rate / Pos_Slew_Rate / Final_Fueling_Offset / 47RE_GR / Manual_GR0 / GR1 / GR2 at e2m 0x018A5700..0x018A5710 = our 0x408d26..0x408d36 (e2m = ours + 0x149C9DA, the block's own delta; the HSG delta 0xCFC008 does not apply); Torque_Mgmt_Fueling / Torque_Mgmt_Required at e2m 0x018A5800 / 02 = our 0x40b61c / 0x40b61e (e2m = ours + 0x149A1E4); Torque_Mgmt_Engine_Speed_Axis / Alpha_Axis / Fueling_Table (21 rpm x 2 alpha) = ROM 0x5b4d6 / 0x5b502 / 0x5b508 (21 rpm breakpoints, alpha axis 0 and 16384, 2 x 21 grid; dimensions and order match, no delta applies to ROM tables). Gear_Down_Active (0x018B8906) / Gear_Down_Gear_Ratio (0x018B8B00) are road speed governor words (RSG_Reference_Speed, SR_Reference_Speed, 'down from top gear') with NO offset match to anything here: the W8 gear-down reading is rejected. e2m 40 ms is the e2m's own statement of the pass period (Torque_Mgmt_Neg_Slew_Rate / Pos_Slew_Rate 'every 40 ms', Torque_Mgmt_Delay_Time scale 0.04 s); the code only counts passes. NOT in use here ('off in this calibration', not dead code): engine_feature_enable_flags_cal = 0x27EF and protection_feature_flags = 0x67BE both have mask 0x1000 clear (disassembly: rlwinm r,r,0,19,19 at 0x3ed20 / 0x3ed74 / 0x3f2c8 / 0x3f2d8) and transmission_type_cal = 3 (48RE) makes cm848_runTorqueManagement store 0x1700 (no limit) before anything else; RAM dump 0: required 0, stage 3, limit 5888.

[W9 item 1 - enable bits, with one e2m mismatch] The two flag words are the e2m algorithm-enable words: the e2m enable table 0x01106B02 + 2 x n matches our 0x3fd59c + 2 x n (algorithm_enable_flags_6_cal 0x3fd5a8 = n 6 = e2m 0x01106B0E, combustion_override_and_estimation_enable_flags_cal 0x3fd5a6 = n 5 = 0x01106B0C), so engine_feature_enable_flags_cal 0x3fd5ec = n 40 = e2m 0x01106B52, protection_feature_flags 0x3fd5f0 = n 42 = 0x01106B56, fuel_feature_control_flags 0x3fd5f2 = n 43 = 0x01106B58. Agreeing bits (code mask = e2m mask): 0x3fd5ec bit 0x4 OPG_Enable (low oil pressure, the oil pressure processing bit), 0x40 J1850_Communication_Enable (the PCI message timeouts bit), 0x1000 Torque_Mgmt_Enable (this cluster), 0x2000 Trip_Info_Enable (the trip counters bit); 0x3fd5f0 bit 0x4 HPCR_Fuelpr_Crank_Mode_Enable (the setpoint cranking phase), 0x20 TC_Stall_Enable (the converter slip monitor gate), 0x40 J1939_Lost_TSC_No_Broadcast_Enable (the datalink_broadcast_enable_flags 0xfff3 shut-off beside fuel_demand_timing_enable_flag), 0x200 Torque_Mgmt_Cold_Increment_Enable (cold delta fuel added to the table limit: fuel_demand_offset_correction = Cold_Delta_Fuel). MISMATCH: e2m Torque_Mgmt_GR_Enable is mask 0x0800 of 0x01106B56 (description cut off: 'Enable to'), but the code tests protection_feature_flags & 0x1000 (rlwinm 0,19,19, verified) for the gear-ratio stage thresholds; e2m lists nothing at 0x400 / 0x1000 for that word. The code mask is the fact; the name of that bit (a manual-transmission gear ratio stage enable) is left to the caller. Comment suggestions: engine_feature_enable_flags_cal 'bit 12 (0x1000) torque management enable (e2m Torque_Mgmt_Enable; off here)'; protection_feature_flags 'bit 12 (0x1000) the manual transmission gear ratio stages of torque management; bit 9 (0x200) cold delta fuel added to the torque management table limit (e2m Torque_Mgmt_Cold_Increment_Enable); bit 5 (0x20) converter stall torque management (e2m TC_Stall_Enable); bit 6 (0x40) J1939 broadcast shut-off on lost TSC1 (e2m J1939_Lost_TSC_No_Broadcast_Enable); bit 2 (0x4) crank rail pressure table (e2m HPCR_Fuelpr_Crank_Mode_Enable)'.

plate_comment: Decides whether torque management is required this pass (torque_management_required_flag) and which table stage applies (torque_management_gear_ratio_stage): manual transmission (transmission_type_cal 0) compares drivetrain_ratio with the manual threshold and, with protection_feature_flags bit 0x1000, the three stage thresholds; type 1 uses the manual threshold while fuel_demand_timing_enable_flag is 1; type 2 (47RE) is required in gear 4, or in unknown gear 255 at or below the 47RE threshold; type 3 only stores a mode word and is never reached. Only called by cm848_runTorqueManagement. (was cm848_evaluateThermalProtectionActive)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40689): the writes are 0x40b61e (flag) and 0x3fb4fe (stage 0 / 1 / 2 / 3); the three stage thresholds and the manual / 47RE thresholds are the e2m Torque_Mgmt_Manual_GR0..GR2 / Manual_GR / 47RE_GR words (see the reading note). The drivetrain ratio is engine speed over vehicle speed x 2048; that it equals the transmission gear ratio is an inference from the e2m names (11530 = 5.63 equals the 5.63:1 first gear of the NV5600 6-speed manual - outside knowledge, not from the firmware; 8192 / 4096 / 1741 = 4.0 / 2.0 / 0.85).

plate_comment: Computes torque_management_table_fuel_limit: stage 3 is a 2-D lookup of engine speed and combustion_alpha_input in the torque management table (ROM 0x5b508, 2944 = 200 mm3 everywhere in this calibration); stages 0-2 read the two 4-D fuelling table sets at throttle breakpoint (stage) over engine speed and blend them by thermal_fuel_limit_factor, skipping a set when the factor is 0 or 0x4000. Adds fuel_demand_offset_correction when protection_feature_flags bit 0x200 is set. (was cm848_calculateThermalLimitValue)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40760); mask 0x200 verified (rlwinm 0,22,22 at 0x3f024); table dumps: x axis 21 rpm breakpoints (1060 - 3035 rpm), alpha axis {0, 16384}, grid 2944 x 42; the stage 0-2 tables are identical pairs here (4 throttle rows 0 / 100 / 200 / 400 counts of 0.25 percent, row 0 all zero, row 1 peaks at 515, row 2 at 1030, row 3 at 2134 counts).

plate_comment: On the pass torque management stops being required, reloads torque_management_exit_delay_timer from torque_management_exit_delay_time; while the timer is nonzero it holds the limit at the previous pass's torque_management_fuel_limit_previous and counts the timer down. (was cm848_processThermalDelayTimer)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40812); e2m Torque_Mgmt_Delay_Time 'delay time for fueling transition from torq mgmt to full fueling' is the reload word 0x408d26 (0 in this ROM).

plate_comment: Sets torque_management_exit_ramp_flag when torque management stops being required; once the exit delay timer is 0 the limit rises each pass by torque_management_fuel_increase_step from the previous pass limit, and the flag clears when the limit exceeds fuel_demand_computed plus torque_management_final_fuel_offset. (was cm848_processThermalRecovery)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40831); e2m Torque_Mgmt_Pos_Slew_Rate 'amount by which fuel will be increased every 40 ms when exiting' = 0x408d2c (75) and Torque_Mgmt_Final_Fueling_Offset 'added to final fueling' = 0x408d2e (74).

plate_comment: Sets torque_management_entry_ramp_flag when torque management becomes required; while it is set the limit is the previous pass fuel demand (first pass) or limit (later passes) minus torque_management_fuel_decrease_step, floored at 0, and the flag clears when the limit would fall below torque_management_table_fuel_limit, which then becomes the limit. (was cm848_processThermalProtectionState)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40853); e2m Torque_Mgmt_Neg_Slew_Rate 'amount by which fuel will be reduced every 40 ms when entering' = 0x408d2a (2950 = 200 mm3, so the first pass already drops far).

plate_comment: With no ramp and no exit delay running: the limit is 0x1700 (5888, the full fuel quantity: no limit) while torque management is not required and torque_management_table_fuel_limit while it is. (was cm848_calculateThermalFuelLimit)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40887).

plate_comment: Torque management pass (cm848_periodicTaskSet_protection): when neither enable bit 0x1000 (engine_feature_enable_flags_cal, protection_feature_flags) is set, or transmission_type_cal is 3, the limit is 0x1700 (no limit); otherwise it evaluates the requirement, the table limit, the exit delay, the exit ramp and the entry ramp, selects the limit and stores the previous-pass copies. Off in this calibration. (was cm848_processThermalProtection)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40907); mask disassembly at 0x3f2c8 / 0x3f2d8 (rlwinm 0,19,19); type test lha 0x3fd934 at 0x3f2e8.

plate_comment: If torque_management_fuel_limit is below the running fuel limit torque_derate_fuel_quantity, takes it and records source code 45 (0x2d) in torque_derate_fuel_source_code; called from cm848_processProtectionLimits (cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit also takes the minimum with torque_management_fuel_limit directly). (was cm848_applyThermalFuelLimit)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40934); caller cpp 43026.

plate_comment: Boot initialization of torque management: required flag, previous required flag and both ramp flags 0, the limit and its previous-pass copies 0x1700 (no limit), the two table lookup cache words 2 and stage 3 (none). (was cm848_initThermalProtectionState)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 40950); called from cm848_applicationMain (cpp 55433).

plate_comment: Boot initialization of the converter slip engine speed limit: both words of its table lookup cache (engine_speed_limit_converter_slip_interpolation_state and the word after it, 0x3fb4ea) are 2 and engine_speed_limit_converter_slip is engine_speed_limit_default_cal. (was mpc555_initThermalProtectionFilters)
evidence: Not part of torque management at all (the W8 note and the old name both put it in this cluster): the three stores are the cache of the converter slip table lookup and the limit cm848_monitorConverterSlipAndEngineSpeedLimit (source 13) writes just above it; disasm_func.py: sth r3,2(r4) at 0x3ecb4 with r4 = 0x3fb4e8, width word. Called from cm848_applicationMain (cpp 55496).

Uncertain, no rename. It is a stw of 5 at 0x3fb500 (disasm 0x3ecd4; the low word 0x3fb502 = 5); xref_addr.py reports 0 references only because the cpp prints it as _subsystem_init_code (underscore overlap). A raw scan of both banks for the low half 0xb500 / 0xb502 finds no reader of either word (the other 0xb500 hits 0x290e8 lhz and 0x3afb0 sth belong to other base addresses; 0xb502 hits are the ROM pointer 0x5b502 and unrelated byte accesses). Its only caller is the transmission_type_cal = 3 branch of cm848_evaluateTorqueManagementRequired, which cm848_runTorqueManagement never reaches (it returns for type 3 first), so the call is unreachable; the word 0x3fb500 is in the time-shared window, so no type or name change is proposed for subsystem_init_code (0x3fb500).

plate_comment: Boot reset of the transmission temperature stability check: clears the unchanged-reading latch (rate_limit_flags bit 2), the previous raw reading and the unchanged-reading counter, and sets transmission_temperature_early_substitute_countdown to 10. (was cm848_resetEngineLoadTracker)
evidence: Read in full (cpp 41076); it touches only the words cm848_selectTransmissionTemperatureInUse uses; called once from cm848_applicationMain (cpp 55540).

Copy of torque_management_required_flag stored at the end of cm848_runTorqueManagement; the edge detectors compare it with the new flag (1 -> 0 starts the exit delay and ramp, 0 -> 1 the entry ramp). Dump 0. Time-shared window: raw scan of the low half 0xb4f0 finds only the cluster (0x3f060 / 0x3f0bc / 0x3f158 / 0x3f338 / 0x3f39c), nothing below 0x7F60.

Previous pass copy of torque_management_fuel_limit (stored at the end of cm848_runTorqueManagement; the exit hold and ramp and the entry ramp start from it). Dump 0x1700. Cluster only (raw scan of 0xb4f2: 0x3f09c / 0x3f110 / 0x3f1bc / 0x3f348 / 0x3f3b0; the 0x3aa54 hit is a stb to another address).

Previous pass copy of fuel_demand_computed (stored at the end of cm848_runTorqueManagement); the first pass of the entry ramp starts from it. Dump 0x1700. Cluster only (raw scan of 0xb4f4: 0x3f19c / 0x3f328 / 0x3f3b8; 0x3a4e0 is an unrelated addi).

Set when torque management stops being required (cm848_rampTorqueManagementFuelLimitUpOnExit), cleared when the rising limit passes fuel_demand_computed plus the final offset; while it is set and the exit delay is over the limit rises by torque_management_fuel_increase_step per pass. Dump 0. Cluster only (raw scan of 0xb4f6).

Set when torque management becomes required (cm848_rampTorqueManagementFuelLimitDownOnEntry), cleared when the falling limit reaches torque_management_table_fuel_limit; while it is set the limit falls by torque_management_fuel_decrease_step per pass. Dump 0. Cluster only (raw scan of 0xb4f8: 0x3f160 / 0x3f24c / 0x3f290 / 0x3f3dc; the 0x3a9c4 hit is a stb elsewhere).

Loaded from torque_management_exit_delay_time on the pass torque management stops being required and counted down once per pass (cm848_holdTorqueManagementFuelLimitDuringExitDelay); the limit is held at the previous pass limit while it is nonzero. The old name says 'entry' but the load is on the falling edge: this is the exit delay. Dump 0 (and the calibration value is 0).

Output of cm848_calculateTorqueManagementFuelTableLimit: the fuel quantity limit from the torque management table or the 4-D tables (plus the cold delta fuel when protection_feature_flags bit 0x200 is set); the limit steady state while torque management is required and the floor of the entry ramp. e2m: Torque_Mgmt_Fueling is the final limit (0x40b61c), this is its table input. Dump 0 (not required). Cluster only (raw scan of 0xb4fc: 0x3f014 / 0x3f1f8 / 0x3f2a4).

Stage chosen by cm848_evaluateTorqueManagementRequired: 0 / 1 / 2 = the manual transmission ratio is at or above stage 0 / 1 / 2 threshold (the 4-D fuelling table is read at throttle breakpoint 0 / 1 / 2, e2m 'use 4D table bpkt 0 / 1 / 2'), 3 = no stage (the torque management table, or not required). Dump 3. Cluster only (raw scan of 0xb4fe: seven hits, all 0x3eda0..0x3f3e8).

Lookup cache (x segment offset, the next word is y) of the stage 3 table in cm848_calculateTorqueManagementFuelTableLimit (cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation, cache pointer argument); set to 2 by cm848_initializeTorqueManagement. Label only. Cluster only; no user below 0x7F60 (cluster hits only).

Second word (y segment offset) of the same lookup cache; set to 2 by cm848_initializeTorqueManagement and never accessed otherwise (the lookup routine updates it through the cache pointer). Label only.

The torque management fuel quantity limit: 0x1700 (5888, no limit) unless required or in a ramp / exit delay; read by cm848_applyTorqueManagementFuelLimit (running limit with source 45) and as one of the minima in cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit (cpp 20729). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Fueling (0x018A5800 = ours + 0x149A1E4): 'fueling limit as calculated by Torque Mgmt algorithm'. Dump 5888. Written only in the cluster (cpp 40822-40965).

1 when the vehicle conditions require torque management (cm848_evaluateTorqueManagementRequired): the output that drives the limit; e2m Torque_Mgmt_Required (0x018A5802 = ours + 0x149A1E4, right after Torque_Mgmt_Fueling like 0x40b61c / 0x40b61e) 'vehicle conditions are met that require torque mgmt'. Dump 0. Ten accesses, all in 0x3ed5c-0x3f394 (cluster).

Reload value of torque_management_exit_delay_timer (passes of the periodic task; e2m Torque_Mgmt_Delay_Time 'delay time for fueling transition from torq mgmt to full fueling', scale 0.04 s, so 40 ms per pass by the e2m). 0 here. Address 0x408d26 is ROM-copied (not in the EEPROM window 0x3fd482-0x3feec1), so the _cal goes. First word of the e2m block (0x018A5700).

drivetrain_ratio (x 2048) at or above which a manual transmission - or type 1 while fuel_demand_timing_enable_flag is 1 - needs torque management (also when vehicle_speed is 0): 11530 = 5.63 - which equals the 5.63:1 first gear of the NV5600 6-speed manual (outside knowledge; reading drivetrain_ratio as the transmission gear ratio is an inference from the e2m names). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Manual_GR 'gear ratio above which will cause manual TX to be in torq mgmt', scale 1/2048 like drivetrain_ratio. ROM-copied, no _cal.

Amount the limit falls per pass in the entry ramp (2950 = 200 mm3, so it normally drops straight to the table limit). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Neg_Slew_Rate 'amount by which fuel will be reduced every 40 ms when entering torq mgmt'. Not a dead band: it is subtracted from the previous demand or limit. ROM-copied, no _cal.
Amount the limit rises per pass in the exit ramp (75 = 5.1 mm3). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Pos_Slew_Rate 'amount by which fuel will be increased every 40 ms when exiting torq mgmt'. ROM-copied, no _cal.

Offset added to fuel_demand_computed in the exit ramp end test: the ramp stops when the rising limit exceeds demand plus this (74 = 5.0 mm3). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Final_Fueling_Offset 'torque mgmt fueling offset for positive slew rate limit; added to final fueling'. ROM-copied, no _cal.

For transmission_type_cal 2 with unknown gear (transmission_current_gear 255): torque management is required at or below this drivetrain_ratio (a top gear ratio); in gear 4 it is required regardless. 0 here. e2m Torque_Mgmt_47RE_GR 'gear ratio below which will cause 47RE trans to be in torq mgmt'. ROM-copied, no _cal. The 47RE is the e2m's name for the type 2 automatic (a transmission model, not an abbreviation made up here).

Manual transmission with protection_feature_flags bit 0x1000: drivetrain_ratio at or above this (8192 = 4.0) selects stage 0, the 4-D fuelling table at throttle breakpoint 0 (all zero fuel in this ROM, hence the old 'cutout'). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Manual_GR0 'gear ratio above which will cause manual TX to use 4D table bpkt 0'. ROM-copied, no _cal.
Same for stage 1 (4096 = 2.0; the table row is 25 percent throttle, 342-515 counts = 23-35 mm3). e2m Torque_Mgmt_Manual_GR1. ROM-copied, no _cal.

Same for stage 2 (1741 = 0.85; the table row is 50 percent throttle, 699-1030 counts = 47-70 mm3); below it the stage is 3 and torque management is not required. e2m Torque_Mgmt_Manual_GR2. ROM-copied, no _cal.

Counts passes in cm848_selectTransmissionTemperatureInUse (cpp 41017-41070) in which the raw reading of the transmission temperature slot equals transmission_temperature_adc_previous_reading; at the limit it clears and sets the unchanged-reading latch (rate_limit_flags bit 2); a changed reading clears it and re-forces the sensor value. Cleared by cm848_resetTransmissionTemperatureValidation. Time-shared window: the raw scan of 0xb504 (0x3f640 / 0x3f6d4 / 0x3f720) has no user below 0x7F60. No fuel flow involved.
Consecutive unchanged raw readings (3) after which the stability latch is set. ROM-copied, no _cal. No fuel flow involved.

Reload value (120000) of transmission_temperature_early_substitute_countdown, applied in park / neutral (switch 20, switch_input_state_bits[2] mask 0x10) while the countdown is nonzero. ROM-copied dword, no _cal.

While nonzero a double sensor fault gives transmission_temperature_early_substitute, at 0 the late one; it counts down by one per pass only while the engine is at the governor setpoint, the vehicle is above transmission_temperature_late_substitute_minimum_vehicle_speed and park / neutral is off, is reloaded in park / neutral while nonzero, and starts at 10 (cm848_resetTransmissionTemperatureValidation). Dump 120000 (the cap: the dump was taken in park / neutral). Written only in cm848_selectTransmissionTemperatureInUse and the reset; the 'fuel flow rate' reading of the old name has no fuel input anywhere.

text: [W9 item 1 - things deliberately NOT renamed] (a) The 4-D fuelling tables and their factor, read by torque management and by SIX other functions (cm848_calculateDualAxisFuelLimit, cm848_calculateFuelDemandWithTrim, cm848_processActiveFaultList, cm848_processSpeedSensorCompensation, cm848_throttlePositionProcessing, governorCruiseStateMachine): fuel_demand_rpm_threshold_cal 0x40688a / fuel_demand_rpm_limit_low_cal 0x4068b6 / fuel_demand_rpm_limit_high_cal 0x4068c0 and governor_fuel_table_xaxis_cal 0x406968 / governor_fuel_table_ystart_cal 0x406994 / governor_fuel_table_yend_cal 0x40699e (rpm axis of 21, a throttle axis of 4 = 0 / 25 / 50 / 100 percent, a 4 x 21 fuel grid; identical in the two sets here) with the lookup caches 0x40a8a1 / a3 / a5 / a7 and thermal_fuel_limit_factor 0x40a889 (Q14, 0x4000 = first set only, 0 = second set only; = combustion_alpha_input after the clamp unless fault status bit 0x10). e2m: Steady_State_RPM_Axis_4_D_Fuel / Steady_State_Throttle_Axis_4_D_Fuel / Steady_State_Table_4_D_Fuel and the Transient_* triple (21 values / 4 values / 4 x 21) at e2m 0x01105400-0x01105900, and the block 0x01105300 matches 0x40a887 + n (e2m = ours + 0xCFAA79): Four_D_Fueling +0 = governor_proportional_gain_calc, Fuel_Interp_Factor +2 = thermal_fuel_limit_factor, +8 Filtered_Commanded_Throttle = fuel_demand_ema_tracked, +A the throttle decrease / transient flags = fuel_limit_mode_flags. So these are very probably the steady state (factor 1, 'open road' alpha) and transient (factor 0, 'urban') 4-D fuelling tables and thermal_fuel_limit_factor is Fuel_Interp_Factor; the set order is the e2m order, which the data (equal sets) cannot confirm. That is a re-domaining of the driver demand fuel path and needs its own wave, not a rename of one cluster. (b) fuel_demand_timing_enable_flag 0x40b1ee (read by the type 1 branch): written only by cm848_updateParkNeutralFlagAndTsc1Activity (cpp 69805-69885) and fuel_demand_timing_initialize (1): 1 at boot, set when the TSC1 active-duration counter says TSC1 is lost / intermittent (fault 356 bit 0x10 set, the engine adds the three TSC1 sources to the ignored-request list and, with protection_feature_flags bit 0x40, shuts off the J1939 broadcasts), cleared when TSC1 has been active long enough; candidate j1939_tsc1_ignored_flag - not proposed (the name of the fault is not verified).

evidence: Still uncertain, no new name. CODE (cm848_applySwitchSelectedEngineSpeedLimit): the alternate droop cap engine_speed_limit_droop_cap_alternate_cal replaces engine_speed_limit_droop_cap_cal only when this word is above 1 (signed compare), engine_speed_limit_droop_cap_alternate_disable is 0 and switch 31 is on; one read, never written, EEPROM 0x8b6 (inside the _cal window), dump 1. e2m (corroboration only; its 0x0100xxxx addresses do NOT equal our EEPROM offsets, e.g. e2m 0x01000828 is ASG_Droop_Gain1_2 but our EEPROM 0x828 is an output channel word): the HSG has THREE parameter sets - HSG_Isochronous_Speed / _2 / _3 at 0x0112EA04 / 06 / 08, HSG_Breakpoint_Speed_2 / _3, HSG_Droop_Slope_2 / _3, 'Alternate' - and a fault 'DG0524JC OEM - Alternate droop switch validation fault'; our droop cap pair (0x3fd80e / 0x3fd810) matches the first two isochronous speeds in order and adjacency. That makes 'number of droop parameter sets (1 to 3)' the likeliest meaning, which the code (> 1 enables set 2) does not contradict but does not prove: no code here reads a value of 3. Candidate if the caller accepts the e2m reading: engine_speed_limit_droop_cap_set_count_cal.

Still uncertain, no new name; the reading is now precise. cm848_updateProtectionStateMachine (cpp 21046-21056) stores engine_speed_limit_arbitrated when the winning source number (engine_speed_limit_arbitration.limiting_source_number) is 1 / 2 / 4 / 5 / 12 and engine_speed_limit_reference otherwise, every pass, before it switches on a 3-bit case (bit 4: the governor speed limit output is farther than DAT_0005c366 from the governor integrator high word; bit 2: the fuel limit source governor_fuel_mode_command is 15, or 16 with fault bits 8 / 9 of fault_detected_bits_0_to_15; bit 1: that source list). cm848_processJ1939RxMessage (0x20c64, called from cases 3 only in its twice-evaluated form) turns a FUEL quantity into the engine speed on the droop line: slope x (engine_speed_limit_ramped_maximum_fuel_quantity - fuel) x 8 / 0x8888 + engine_speed_limit_arbitrated (capped at 40000), or this word when the slope is 0 (a vertical droop line), and stores that speed and the fuel in the protection_* threshold words; it is called from case 3 of that switch with protection_output_select_cal or protection_integrator_cal as the fuel argument, which is chosen by comparing this word with DAT_0005c35e. So it is the speed of the droop line when the line has no slope, chosen between the arbitrated limit (limits that act as the governor reference) and the reference limit - 'the engine speed reference of the protection threshold curve'. The protection_* threshold words and the DAT_0005c34c-0005c366 constants form one structure (speed / fuel breakpoint pairs with 'level' variants selected by that 3-bit case) that needs its own wave. Time-shared window; one writer function (two stores) and no boot-ROM user by immediate scan (W8). Candidate: engine_speed_limit_droop_line_reference_speed.

Still uncertain, no name. xref_addr.py: 0 reads / 1 write, a single sth r10 at 0x204a0 in cm848_initializeEngineSpeedLimitDefaults (width WORD); 0x40a282 has no reference at all. So the dword type of the row is wrong - the store is a halfword to 0x40a280 only. text: [W9 item 4 - how far the boot-kernel table really reaches] PROVEN by scans of ROM and flash 2 (kernscan.py in scratch_W9_gear_down). cm848_registerDiagnosticService (0x2c94) has exactly 14 call sites in the whole binary and none in flash 2: ROM 0x398 / 0x3a8 / 0x3bc / 0x3c8 / 0x3d4 (cm848_registerStandardDiagServices: services 2, 7, 11, 16, 24), 0x1934 (cm848_initService25Handler: 25), 0x19a4 / 0x19b4 / 0x19c4 / 0x19d4 (cm848_initDataBasedDiagServices: 68, 69, 75, 77), 0x1ae8 (cm848_registerService65Handler: 65), 0x1b14 / 0x1b24 / 0x1b34 (cm848_registerMemoryReadServices: 67, 74, 76); no plain b targets it. cm848_dispatchDiagnosticService (0x6d24) has one direct call (ROM 0x60f8 in mpc555_handleJ1939TransportDataPacket); its RAM copy (&DAT_003fc8f4) is also passed to cm848_registerPgnEf00Handler, so it can additionally run through that registration. The register function refuses entry 21 (count 0x14, returns true), so the CAPACITY is 20 entries x 5 bytes = 100 bytes, 0x3fdb30-0x3fdb93, and the count byte diag_scan_step_counter 0x3fdb94 follows the table directly; only 14 entries are ever registered, so the REAL REACH is 14 x 5 = 70 bytes, 0x3fdb30-0x3fdb75 (entry n: service id byte at 0x3fdb30 + 5n, 4-byte handler pointer at +1, unaligned). Every instruction in ROM 0x0-0x7f5f carrying a displacement 0xdb30-0xdb94 (load / store / addi / ori / andi forms): ONLY 0x2c98 (addi 0xdb94: the count, register function), 0x2cb4 (addi 0xdb30: the base there), 0x6d3c (addi 0xdb30, dispatch) and 0x6d6c (lbz 0xdb94, the count in dispatch); both functions index the table as base + 5n, so the kernel makes no constant-offset access into it. Everything else in 0x3fdb30-0x3fdb93 is application data: the RAM dump window equals the EEPROM image at 0x6ae-0x711 byte for byte (0x3fdb30 = EEPROM 0x6ae; compared all 100 bytes; the count byte is 0), so in the running application the kernel table is completely overwritten by the EEPROM mirror - the two uses of the RAM are time-shared, never concurrent.
